NJ-WT New Jersey Income Tax Withholding Instructions (September 2025): "If the supplemental wages are paid at a different time: • Withhold from the supplemental wages without any exemption allowances your employee takes on the NJ- W4."

notes: New Mexico top marginal 5.9%.
supplemental_note: FYI-104 New Mexico Withholding Tax (Rev. 11/2024): "If the federal withholding is calculated using a flat percent, a flat 5.9% of the supplemental wage or fringe benefit amount should be withheld for state tax purposes." Otherwise follow the federal method.

notes: Nevada has no state personal income tax.
New York top marginal 10.9% (millionaires' tax). NYC and Yonkers add separately — see payroll_local_income_tax.
supplemental_note: 20 NYCRR 171.4, as amended for supplemental wages paid after December 31, 2021 (adopted rule text): an employer "may withhold New York State personal income tax from the supplemental wages at a rate equal to the rate of New York State personal income tax to be withheld from the highest denominated taxable income", 11.70 percent. State rate only.

notes: Ohio top marginal 3.125% for tax year 2025 (income over $100,000; 2.75% from $26,050 to $100,000; nothing below) — ORC 5747.02(A)(3). 3.5% was the 2024 top rate. Municipalities add separately — see payroll_local_income_tax.
supplemental_note: Ohio Adm. Code 5703-7-10 (effective February 3, 2024, in force through 2025): employers withhold "From its employees' supplemental compensation, subject to the tax imposed by Chapter 5747. of the Revised Code, at a flat rate of at least three and one-half per cent". That is 3.5%, a required minimum.

notes: Oklahoma top marginal 4.75%.
supplemental_note: Okla. Admin. Code 710:90-1-6(b)(1): if tax was withheld from regular wages, "(A) Withhold at the highest applicable rate set out in 68 O.S. Section 2355(B)(1) for Oklahoma Income Taxes for the taxable year", or use the aggregate method. The rule prints no number; 4.75% is the top rate in the 2025 OW-2 withholding tables.

notes: Oregon top marginal 9.9%.
supplemental_note: Oregon Withholding Tax Formulas, 150-206-436 (Rev. 12-10-24): "Employers may use a 8 percent flat rate to figure withholding on supplemental wages that are paid at a different time than an employee's regular payday."

notes: Pennsylvania flat 3.07% (long-standing). Local EIT/LST add separately — see payroll_local_income_tax.
supplemental_note: REV-415 Employer Withholding Information Guide (01-23): "If an employee receives supplemental or other com- pensation, an employer must determine the tax to withhold by adding the supplemental or other compensation for the current payroll period and multiplying this amount by the withholding rate." Pennsylvania has one flat rate, 3.07%, for all compensation.

notes: Rhode Island top marginal 5.99%.
supplemental_note: 2025 Rhode Island Employer's Income Tax Withholding Tables: "The Supplemental withholding rate is 5.99%."

notes: South Carolina top marginal 6.2% in 2025 (reduced from 7%).
supplemental_note: Not verified: the South Carolina withholding formula (WH-1603F, 2025) and guide say nothing about supplemental wages. Use the state's regular withholding tables, or check its current withholding guide, for bonuses and other supplemental wages.

notes: South Dakota has no state personal income tax.
Tennessee has no state personal income tax (Hall tax repealed 2021).
Texas has no state personal income tax.
Utah flat 4.5% for tax year 2025 (4.55% was the 2024 rate) — Utah State Tax Commission tax rates.
supplemental_note: Not verified: Utah Publication 14 (2025) says nothing about supplemental wages. Use the state's regular withholding tables, or check its current withholding guide, for bonuses and other supplemental wages.

notes: Virginia top marginal 5.75%.
supplemental_note: Virginia Income Tax Withholding Guide for Employers (Rev. 05/25; archived copy of the official file): "if supplemental wage payments are paid and tax has been withheld from the employee's regular wages, the employer may determine the tax to be withheld by using a flat percentage rate of 5.75%, without allowance for exemption and without reference to any regular payment of wages." Optional.

notes: Vermont top marginal 8.75%.
supplemental_note: No flat supplemental rate on wages. Vermont GB-1210 (2025): "For non- periodic payments, the Vermont withholding can be estimated at 30% of the federal withholding." That is a share of the federal amount, not a percentage of the payment.

notes: Washington has no state personal income tax (capital-gains tax only).
Wisconsin top marginal 7.65%.
supplemental_note: No single supplemental rate. Wisconsin Publication W-166 (6/24; archived copy of the official file): "the withholding on supplemental wage payments may be determined by estimating the employee's annual gross salary and applying flat percentages to the supplemental payments." The rate depends on the salary bracket: 3.54%, 4.65%, 5.30% or 7.65%.

notes: West Virginia top marginal 4.82% in 2025 (reduced from 6.5%).
supplemental_note: No flat supplemental rate: the state withholds on supplemental wages with its regular tables or formula. West Virginia Tax Division, Withholding Help: "Supplemental payments would then be the excess of that using the annual table as published by the Tax Division."

notes: Wyoming has no state personal income tax.
